entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Hélène Moszkiewiez was a Jewish Belgian woman who went undercover as a secretary at Gestapo headquarters in Brussels during World War II. In her two years as a clerk, she gathered arrest and deportation lists from the Nazis for the British intelligence and Belgian Resistance, giving them the opportunity to warn or evacuate targeted people. Following the war, she moved to Vancouver, where she lived until her death.
